title: WebCrypto Key Storage
description: Stores keys in the browser's WebCrypto store marked non-extractable, so JavaScript can use them but never read the raw bytes. Even a cross-site scripting flaw cannot exfiltrate a key it cannot see, which sharply limits what client-side attacks can steal.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: IndexedDB Key Vaults
description: Keeps wrapped keys in IndexedDB, encrypted under a device key the page cannot export. The vault persists across sessions without ever exposing plaintext keys to page scripts, giving web apps durable client-side key storage.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Key Rotation
description: Replaces keys on a schedule - every 90 days is typical - and re-encrypts data under the new key, limiting how much any single compromised key can expose. Rotation is automated so it actually happens, with the old key retained briefly for decrypting in-flight data.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Passphrase-Derived Keys
description: Derives encryption keys from a user passphrase with a memory-hard KDF and a random salt, so no key is ever stored anywhere. Forgetting the passphrase means losing the data - which is exactly the security property that makes server-side coercion useless.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Biometric-Bound Keys
description: Ties key use to a biometric check performed in the secure enclave, so the key only operates after the device verifies its owner. The biometric itself never leaves the enclave - it merely unlocks the key for that one operation.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Key Export and Backup
description: Exports keys only as encrypted blobs protected by a recovery passphrase, letting users back up keys without ever seeing them in the clear. The export format is versioned and documented so future software can still import decade-old backups.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Hardware Security Keys
description: Uses physical FIDO2 security keys for authentication, where the private key is generated on the key and never leaves it. Phishing fails because the key cryptographically verifies the site's identity before signing anything.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Session Keys
description: Issues short-lived keys for each session that expire automatically, so a stolen session key is useful only briefly. Sessions re-authenticate transparently in the background, keeping the user experience smooth while the exposure window stays tiny.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Key Usage Policies
description: Attaches policies to each key - which operations it may perform, until when, from which origins - enforced by the keystore itself. A signing key cannot suddenly be used for decryption no matter what the calling code asks for.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-Device Sync
description: Syncs keys across a user's devices through end-to-end encrypted channels, so a new phone gets the keys without any server ever seeing them. Device pairing uses short codes verified out-of-band to prevent man-in-the-middle during enrollment.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Key Revocation
description: Revokes compromised keys immediately and publishes the revocation to all devices, which stop trusting the key within minutes. Revocation lists are signed and timestamped so devices can verify them even when the network is hostile.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Wrapping Keys
description: Protects data keys by encrypting them under a wrapping key that lives in the most secure store available. The hierarchy means only the wrapping key needs hardware protection; everything below it inherits that protection through encryption.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Key Audit Logs
description: Records every key operation - creation, use, rotation, destruction - in a tamper-evident log the key owner can review. Audit logs reveal misuse patterns like a signing key suddenly used at 3 AM from an unusual origin.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Recovery Codes
description: Issues single-use recovery codes at setup that can restore access if all devices are lost. Codes are shown once, meant to be printed and stored physically, and each use is logged so a stolen code's misuse is visible.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Least-Privilege Key Scopes
description: Issues keys scoped to the minimum capability needed - a key that can only decrypt one folder, or only sign for one service. Scoped keys contain breaches: a leaked key grants the attacker only its narrow scope, not the kingdom.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
